Here's a brief demo (no pun intended) of Briefer. It may take a few seconds to load.

The recommended way to run Briefer locally is to install it using `pip` and run it using the `briefer` command. Please note that Briefer requires Docker to run, so make sure you have it installed before running the commands below.
If you run Briefer using `pip`, our initialization scripts will take care of downloading our docker image, setting up volumes to store Briefer's data, and starting the application.
For more information on how to deploy Briefer in production, please refer to our deployment guide.
If you want to contribute to Briefer, please read our contributing guide which explains how run Briefer in development mode.
Finally, in case you want to use files, you can upload them to Briefer and read them in Python or query them using SQL thanks to our DuckDB integration.
The `web` is the main interface of Briefer. It's where you create and edit your notebooks and dashboards. The `web` is a Next.js application that communicates with the `api` to fetch and save data.

You can read more about our licensing decisions and open-source philosophy in this blog post. To summarise, we'll aim to include all data-related features in the open-source version and save integrations and granular permissions for the cloud version.
Can I use the cloud version for free instead?
You can sign up for the cloud version here and read more about our pricing in our pricing page.
What are the differences between the open-source and cloud versions?

The main difference between the open-source and cloud versions is that the cloud version is a hosted service that we maintain and update. Additionally, the cloud version supports multiple workspaces, has more granular permissions, email and Slack integrations. Our enterprise tier also includes SSO.
How easy is it to self-serve in Briefer?

Still, we don't believe that _any_ tool can be 100% self-serve. That's because even if people manage to create a query and fetch data, non-technical users usually can't validate or interpret the results without some context. We've written a detailed blog post about this theme here.
How can I get in touch?
You can reach out to us on Slack or by email at founders@briefer.cloud.
